name: Plink
what: One drop into still water. A tick, then the bubble's ring climbing and dying inside a fifth of a second.
differs: Ask is small and bright and clearly climbs. Done is a heavier drop, lower, with the water's own thump under it.

name: Cistern
what: The same drop inside a stone cistern: a short, damped tail says the room is small and wet.
differs: Same pair as Plink, an octave lower and in a room. The longest of the water options.

name: Drip and answer
what: Two drops, the second answering the first. Drips come in pairs, and a pair reads as a cue rather than a ping.
differs: Ask: the second drop is higher, so the pair rises. Done: the second is lower and heavier, so the pair falls and lands.

name: Pebble
what: A pebble into deep water. A bigger bubble rings lower and longer, and the splash has more body.
differs: Ask climbs a full octave. Done barely climbs and sits on a low thump: something went in and the water closed over it.

name: Bamboo
what: A hollow wooden knock, the deer-scarer in a garden. Not water: the one dry option, and the least likely to wear out.
differs: Ask is one knock, high. Done is a lower knock and the arm rocking back, softer.

name: Bird
what: A small whistle, two notes. The most 'alive' of the six and the riskiest: a voice in the room every time the agent asks.
differs: Ask: two notes rising, tu-wee. Done: two notes falling, wee-oo.
